title: The Wednesday
isolates: event risk and rule integrity under drawdown
_source: Extracted from docs/tiq/reference/decision-sim.html. Deterministic fields (account, rules, opening_position, scripts, settle_t, option acts/points) are consumed by shared/tiq/sim.js. Node beats/questions and option prose are carried as data for the (deferred) Workbench surface; the engine ignores them.
_conditions: Node variants branch on user STATE, never on the market. 'flat' = no open lots; 'holding' = at least one open lot. 'clean'/'broken' = whether any rule has been broken. Beat tokens like {unreal:t1} are filled deterministically by the renderer from sim.js (unrealised at that time); the market path itself is fixed.

script_labels.B: The other Wednesday — SPY keeps falling

confidence_scale.label: Certain — I do this every time
Not sure, it could go either way

nodes.beat: Your SPY 590/585 put spread is showing 56% of maximum profit with 12 days left. You sold three of them for 0.80. Your written rule closes at 50%. That trigger fired yesterday. The Fed decides at 19:00 tonight.
nodes.question: What do you do?

options.text: Close all three. The rule fired
Close two, run one through the Fed
Hold all three. The setup still looks fine
Hold, and sell two more while premium is rich

beat_variants.flat: Hawkish hold. SPY dropped 1.8% in nine minutes. Volatility is bid across the board — the spread you closed this morning at 0.35 is now marked 1.05. You are flat. Premium is the richest it has been in three weeks.
beat_variants.holding: Hawkish hold. SPY dropped 1.8%. Your spread is marked 1.05 against the 0.80 you collected — you are down {unreal:t1}. Your stop sits at 2× credit, which is 1.60. You are not there yet.

question_variants.flat: Premium is rich and you have capital. What do you do?

flat.text: Nothing tonight. Look tomorrow with a plan
Open a new spread — this is exactly the volatility you wait for
Re-enter the same trade you just closed, bigger
flat.breaks: re-entered a closed trade on impulse

holding.text: Hold. The stop has not been hit
Close now and take the loss
Roll down and out for a small credit
Sell two more at 1.05 — better prices than this morning

beat_variants.flat: SPY opened another 0.7% lower. The spread you are no longer in is marked 1.50. Had you held from yesterday morning you would be down roughly {heldLoss:t2}. You are flat and it is 09:31.
beat_variants.holding: SPY gapped lower again. Your spread is marked 1.50. That is 1.88× the credit. Your stop is 2×. Open loss: {unreal:t2}. That is {pctOfAccount:t2}% of the account.

flat.text: Stay flat. You have no setup and no plan for today
Sell a spread now — this is the fattest premium of the month
Sell a spread, double size, to make back yesterday

holding.text: Hold. The stop is 2× and this is 1.88×
Close now. It is close enough to the stop
Sell three more at 1.50. The premium is enormous
holding.breaks: doubled a loser inside a drawdown

beat_variants.clean: NVDA is up 6.2% on a supply headline. It was not on your watchlist this morning. Its options went from cheap to expensive in an hour. Your day has gone to plan so far. Your group chat has four entries posted in it.
beat_variants.broken: NVDA is up 6.2% on a supply headline. It was not on your watchlist this morning. Its options went from cheap to expensive in an hour. You are already having a difficult two days. Your group chat has four entries posted in it.

options.text: Nothing. Write down what a valid NVDA entry would look like and set an alert
Take a small defined-risk position to be involved
Sell an NVDA spread — the premium is genuinely rich now
Wait for it to come back to this morning's price, then buy

beat_variants.flat: SPY reversed hard into the close and finished the day up 1.4%. You are flat. Realised so far: {cash}. Tomorrow you have three setups on the watchlist. Your standard risk is 2% per trade.
beat_variants.holding: SPY reversed hard into the close and finished the day up 1.4%. Your position is marked 0.55. Open P&L {unreal:t3}. Tomorrow you have three setups on the watchlist. Your standard risk is 2% per trade.

broken.text: Skip tomorrow entirely and review the last two days

options.text: 3% — the last two days cost me and there is ground to make up
